Django News

News

The news app: publications, articles, and newsletters, the rules for who may see and change them, and the site’s pages.

news.models

The news app’s models: publications, articles, and newsletters.

Each model sets its own table name, such as publication, in place of Django’s default, such as news_publication.

class news.models.Publication(*args, **kwargs)[source]

A news outlet, owned by a publisher and staffed by editors and journalists.

Working for a publication gives an editor or journalist rights over its articles and newsletters. Being removed from its staff ends them.

Variables:

  • owner – The publisher who owns the publication.

  • name – The publication’s name, unique across the site.

  • description – A description of the publication.

  • editors – The editors who work for the publication.

  • journalists – The journalists who work for the publication.

class news.models.Article(*args, **kwargs)[source]

A news article written by a journalist, either for a publication or independently.

It must be approved before readers can see it.

Variables:

  • title – The article’s title.

  • content – The article’s text.

  • author – The journalist who wrote the article. Never changes.

  • publication – The publication the article is for, or None for an independent article. Set when the article is created and never changed, except that deleting the publication makes the article independent.

  • created_at – When the article was created.

  • approved – Whether the article has been approved. Once an article is approved, it is never set back to pending.

class news.models.Newsletter(*args, **kwargs)[source]

A curated collection of approved articles, created by a journalist, either for a publication or independently.

Variables:

  • title – The newsletter’s title.

  • description – A description of the newsletter.

  • author – The journalist who created the newsletter. Never changes.

  • publication – The publication the newsletter is for, or None for an independent newsletter. Set when the newsletter is created and never changed. Deleting the publication deletes its newsletters.

  • created_at – When the newsletter was created.

  • articles – The articles in the newsletter. Approved articles only: the publication’s articles, or, for an independent newsletter, the author’s own independent articles.

news.access

Access rules for who may see, change, approve, and manage content.

Every page and API view follows them by calling these functions, so each rule is written once and no two pages can disagree.

Group permissions decide which kinds of actions a role may take. These functions decide which publications, articles, and newsletters each action applies to. A user’s rights over a publication’s content come from working for it now, so a former editor or journalist has none.

news.access.publications_user_can_manage(user, permission)[source]

The publications a user may edit or delete.

A publication is included when all of these are true:

  • The user has the permission. Only the Publishers group has it.

  • The owner of the publication is the user.

Parameters:

  • user – User object

  • permission – The permission the user must have, such as news.change_publication

Returns:

A queryset of Publication objects.

news.access.articles_visible_to(user)[source]

Distinct articles the user may read.

An article is included when any one of these is true:

  • The article has been approved.

  • The author of the article is the user, and the article is not assigned to a publication.

  • The user is an editor of the article’s publication.

  • The user is a journalist of the article’s publication.

Publishers and readers see only approved articles.

Parameters:

user – User object

Returns:

A queryset of Article objects.

news.access.subscribed_articles(reader)[source]

Approved articles from the reader’s subscriptions.

An article is included when it is approved, and any one of these is true:

  • Its publication is one the reader subscribes to.

  • Its author is a journalist the reader subscribes to, and the article is not assigned to a publication. A subscription to a journalist covers only their independent articles.

Parameters:

reader – User object

Returns:

A queryset of Article objects.

news.access.articles_user_can_approve(user)[source]

The pending articles the user may approve.

An article is included when the user has the approve_article permission, the article has not been approved already, and any one of these is true:

  • The user is an editor of the article’s publication.

  • The author of the article is the user, and the article is not assigned to a publication.

Parameters:

user – User object

Returns:

A queryset of Article objects.

news.access.articles_user_can_change(user)[source]

Distinct articles the user may edit or delete.

An article is included when any one of these is true:

  • The author of the article is the user, and the article is not assigned to a publication.

  • The user is an editor of the article’s publication.

  • The user is a journalist of the article’s publication.

Parameters:

user – User object

Returns:

A queryset of Article objects.

news.access.articles_for_newsletter(journalist, publication)[source]

The approved articles that can go in a newsletter.

For an independent newsletter (publication is None), an article is included when all of these are true:

  • The article has been approved.

  • The author of the article is the journalist.

  • The article is not assigned to a publication.

For a publication’s newsletter, an article is included when all of these are true:

  • The article has been approved.

  • The article is assigned to the publication.

Parameters:

  • journalist – User object

  • publication – Publication object, or None for an independent newsletter

Returns:

A queryset of Article objects.

news.access.newsletters_user_can_change(user)[source]

Distinct newsletters the user may edit or delete.

A newsletter is included when any one of these is true:

  • The author of the newsletter is the user, and the newsletter is not assigned to a publication.

  • The user is an editor of the newsletter’s publication.

  • The user is a journalist of the newsletter’s publication.

Parameters:

user – User object

Returns:

A queryset of Newsletter objects.

news.approval

What happens when an article is approved: it is emailed to its subscribers and shared with the third party.

The approval signals in news/signals.py call these functions. If sending an email or reaching the third party fails, the failure is logged, and the approval still stands.

news.approval.THIRD_PARTY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 5

How long to wait for the third party to answer, in seconds, so a slow or missing server cannot hold up an approval.

news.approval.get_recipients(article)[source]

The email addresses of the readers subscribed to an approved article.

A publication article goes to the publication’s subscribers. An independent article goes to its author’s subscribers.

Parameters:

article – The approved Article.

Returns:

A list of the subscribers’ email addresses.

news.approval.notify_subscribers(article)[source]

Emails an approved article to each of its subscribers.

Each reader gets their own copy, so no reader sees the other readers’ addresses. A failure is logged, and the approval still stands.

Parameters:

article – The approved Article.

news.approval.share_article(article)[source]

Sends an approved article to the third-party API as JSON.

It goes to the address in the THIRD_PARTY_API_URL setting, with the THIRD_PARTY_API_KEY setting in the X-API-Key header. If the request fails, times out, or the third party answers with an error, the failure is logged, and the approval still stands.

Parameters:

article – The approved Article.

news.signals

The approval signals, which email an article to its subscribers and share it with the third party when it is approved.

Django calls these handlers before and after every Article is saved. They are connected when the app starts, in NewsConfig.ready().

news.signals.remember_previous_approval(sender, instance, **kwargs)[source]

Before an article is saved, notes whether it was pending, so announce_approval() can tell whether this save approved it.

Parameters:

  • sender – The model being saved, Article.

  • instance – The Article about to be saved.

  • kwargs – The other arguments of Django’s pre_save signal. Not used.

news.signals.announce_approval(sender, instance, **kwargs)[source]

After an article is saved, emails it to its subscribers and shares it with the third party, but only when this save approved it.

Approving from a page, the admin or the API all run this once, and later updates to the article run nothing.

Parameters:

  • sender – The model that was saved, Article.

  • instance – The Article just saved.

  • kwargs – The other arguments of Django’s post_save signal. Not used.

news.forms

The news app’s forms: for writing articles, putting together newsletters, and setting up publications.

class news.forms.ArticleForm(*args, author, **kwargs)[source]

The form for writing a new article or editing one.

A new article can be independent or for a publication its author is on the staff of. Once the article exists, its publication cannot change.

Builds the form for the article’s author, offering only the publications they are on the staff of.

Parameters:

  • author – The User writing the article, or its author when it is being edited.

  • kwargs – Passed on to Django’s ModelForm, such as the instance being edited.

property media

Return all media required to render the widgets on this form.

class news.forms.NewsletterForm(*args, author, **kwargs)[source]

The form for putting together a new newsletter or editing one.

A new newsletter can be independent or for a publication its author is on the staff of. Once the newsletter exists, its publication cannot change.

An independent newsletter can include only its author’s approved independent articles. A publication’s newsletter can include only that publication’s approved articles.

Variables:

author – The newsletter’s author, which clean() uses to check the chosen articles.

Builds the form for the newsletter’s author, offering only the publications and articles they may use.

Parameters:

  • args – Passed on to Django’s ModelForm, such as the submitted data.

  • author – The User putting the newsletter together, or its author when it is being edited.

  • kwargs – Passed on to Django’s ModelForm, such as the instance being edited.

The label beside an article’s checkbox: its title, author, and publication.

Parameters:

news.admin

The news app’s admin pages.

Registers the publications, articles and newsletters, with Django’s default admin pages.

The article pages: the list of approved articles, and the pages for reading, writing, approving, editing, and deleting an article.

news.views.articles.article_list(request)[source]

The list of every approved article on the site, newest first, from all publications and all independent journalists.

Every user sees the same list. It is not limited to the user’s subscriptions. Pending articles are not listed here. They appear on the dashboards of the people who work on them.

Parameters:

request – The HTTP request.

The article list page.

The page for approving a pending article, after a confirmation.

An editor approves the articles of their publication, and a journalist approves their own independent articles. Anyone else gets “404 Not Found”.

Management commands

The migrate_all management command.

Builds or updates every table from the models, in one step. It runs two of Django’s own commands in order:

  1. makemigrations writes a migration file for any model change that does not have one yet.

  2. migrate applies every migration that has not run yet, creating or changing the tables.

On an empty database, such as after drop_all_tables, this creates every table. The role groups and demo data are not part of it; afterward:

python manage.py setup_groups_and_permissions
python manage.py seed_demo_data

How to run it

From the folder that contains manage.py:

python manage.py migrate_all
class news.management.commands.migrate_all.Command(stdout=None, stderr=None, no_color=False, force_color=False)[source]

Run makemigrations, then migrate.

Run it with:

python manage.py migrate_all
handle(*args, **options)[source]

Write any missing migrations, then apply every migration.

Parameters:

  • args – Positional arguments from Django. Not used.

  • options – The command’s options, from Django. Not used.

The seed_demo_data management command.

Fills a blank database with the sample accounts, publications, subscriptions, articles, and newsletters in _demo_data.py, and a superuser for the Django admin, for looking at the site and trying it out by hand. Unit tests do not use it; each test creates its own data.

It only runs on a blank database: one with no users, publications, articles, or newsletters. That is what keeps it simple. It creates everything in one pass, with no checks for what already exists.

How to run it

From the folder that contains manage.py, after migrate_all and setup_groups_and_permissions:

python manage.py seed_demo_data

If the database already has data, empty it first:

python manage.py delete_all_data
python manage.py seed_demo_data
class news.management.commands.seed_demo_data.Command(stdout=None, stderr=None, no_color=False, force_color=False)[source]

Fill a blank database with the demo data in _demo_data.py.

Run it on a blank database, after setup_groups_and_permissions:

python manage.py seed_demo_data

It stops without changing anything if the database already has any users, publications, articles, or newsletters, or if the role groups have not been set up. Everything is created in one transaction, so if anything fails, the database is left blank.

Check that the database is blank, then create the demo data.

  • args – Positional arguments from Django. Not used.

  • options – The command’s options, from Django. Not used.

Raises:

CommandError – If the database is not blank, or the role groups have not been set up yet.

create_users()[source]

Create each account in USERS, and the superuser in SUPERUSER. User.save() puts each one in its role’s group.

The new users, by username. For example, users["Paul"] is the Publisher Paul.

create_articles(users, publications)[source]

Create each article in ARTICLES, dated days_ago days back.

Articles created already approved do not email subscribers or share the article with the third party, since the approval signals only act when a pending article becomes approved.

  • publications – The new publications, by name.

Returns:

backdate(item, days_ago)[source]

Move an article’s or newsletter’s creation date back by a number of days.

created_at is filled in automatically when an item is first saved, and that value cannot be set on creation, so it is changed afterward with update(), which writes straight to the database. For example:

self.backdate(article, 3)  # created three days ago
Parameters:

  • item – The Article or Newsletter just created.

  • days_ago – How many days ago it should say it was created.

The delete_all_data management command.

Deletes every user, publication, article, and newsletter, every article the simulated third party received, and every login session, so the site can start again from empty. The groups and their permissions are kept, since they are setup rather than data.

How to run it

From the folder that contains manage.py:

python manage.py delete_all_data

It asks you to type yes before deleting anything. To skip the question:

python manage.py delete_all_data --no-input

To fill the database again afterward:

python manage.py seed_demo_data

It only runs while DEBUG is True, so it cannot empty a live site.

class news.management.commands.delete_all_data.Command(stdout=None, stderr=None, no_color=False, force_color=False)[source]

Delete every user, publication, article, newsletter, third-party article, and login session.

Run it with:

python manage.py delete_all_data

Superusers are deleted too; seed_demo_data makes the admin superuser again. The groups and their permissions are kept, so seed_demo_data can be run straight afterward.

The drop_all_tables management command.

Deletes every table in the project’s database: all the site’s data, Django’s own tables, and the records of which migrations have run. The database itself is kept, and so are the MariaDB account’s rights to it, so nothing needs setting up again in MariaDB.

Afterward, the database is empty, and the site cannot run until the tables are rebuilt. The usual steps from there:

python manage.py migrate_all
python manage.py setup_groups_and_permissions
python manage.py seed_demo_data

How to run it

From the folder that contains manage.py:

python manage.py drop_all_tables

It asks you to type yes before deleting anything. To skip the question:

python manage.py drop_all_tables --no-input

It only runs while DEBUG is True, so it cannot empty a live site.

class news.management.commands.drop_all_tables.Command(stdout=None, stderr=None, no_color=False, force_color=False)[source]

Delete every table in the project’s database.

Run it with:

python manage.py drop_all_tables

The database and the MariaDB account’s rights to it are kept.

Demo data

The data itself is long, so these entries show what each part is for, not its contents. See _demo_data.py for the full data.

The sample accounts, publications, subscriptions, articles, and newsletters that seed_demo_data loads. This file holds only the data; the command decides how to load it.

The pieces are linked by name: owners, staff, readers, subscribed journalists, and authors are usernames from USERS; publications are names from PUBLICATIONS; and a newsletter’s articles are titles from ARTICLES.

The underscore at the start of the file’s name keeps Django from treating it as a command. Every other .py file in management/commands/ becomes one. seed_demo_data, in the same folder, reads the data with:

from . import _demo_data as demo_data
demo_data.USERS  # the list of accounts
news.management.commands._demo_data.PASSWORD

Every demo account uses this password.

news.management.commands._demo_data.USERS

The demo accounts. Two of each role cover the usual situations, and a few more cover the rest:

"Jonah"   # a Journalist on the staff of both publications
"Jade"    # an independent Journalist, on no publication's staff
"Ezra"    # an Editor on the staff of both publications
"Esther"  # an Editor on no publication's staff
"Rosa"    # a Reader who subscribes to nothing

Each account logs in with its username and the password above.

news.management.commands._demo_data.SUPERUSER

A superuser for the Django admin, with the same password.

news.management.commands._demo_data.GAZETTE

The demo publications’ names, also used in SUBSCRIPTIONS, ARTICLES, and NEWSLETTERS, so a typo raises an error instead of linking to a publication that does not exist.

news.management.commands._demo_data.COURIER

The second demo publication’s name, used the same way as GAZETTE.

news.management.commands._demo_data.PUBLICATIONS

The demo publications, one owned by each demo Publisher. Each has two editors and two journalists on its staff: its own pair, plus Ezra and Jonah, who work for both. The owner, editors, and journalists are usernames from USERS. For example:

"Paul"    # owns The Lamplight Gazette
"Elena"   # edits for The Lamplight Gazette
news.management.commands._demo_data.SUBSCRIPTIONS

What each demo Reader subscribes to. The two Readers subscribe to different things, so each one’s subscribed articles differ. A subscription to a journalist covers only their independent articles, so Rhonda gets Julia’s independent articles through her subscription to Julia, and Julia’s Courier articles through her subscription to The Copper Kettle Courier. Rosa is not listed, so she subscribes to nothing. For example:

"Richard", GAZETTE  # Richard subscribes to The Lamplight Gazette
news.management.commands._demo_data.ARTICLES

The demo articles. James and Julia each write three for their own publication, two approved and one pending, plus two independent articles, one approved and one pending. Jonah writes for both publications, and Jade writes only independent articles. The author is a username from USERS, and publication is None for an independent article. days_ago sets how long ago the article was created, so the lists show different dates. For example:

"publication": GAZETTE  # filed under The Lamplight Gazette
"publication": None     # independent
"days_ago": 3           # created 3 days before the command ran
news.management.commands._demo_data.NEWSLETTERS

The demo newsletters: one for each publication by its own journalist, one each of James’s and Julia’s independent work, and Jonah’s Gazette Weekend Edition, which includes James’s Night Market article, so that article is in two newsletters. The author is a username from USERS, publication is None for an independent newsletter, and articles are titles from ARTICLES. Every article must fit its newsletter: for an independent one, the author’s own approved independent articles; for a publication’s, that publication’s approved articles, whoever wrote them. days_ago sets how long ago the newsletter was created. For example:

"Lamplight After Dark"  # James's newsletter for the Gazette
